text:
maria: Heads-up: multiple reports of the JS SDK failing in edge runtimes after the latest publish. Root cause looks like exports + types mapping.

dan: Repro (Vercel edge): `TypeError: default is not a constructor` when users do `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'`. Named imports work.

shawn: Found that our package.json only had a top-level `types` and basic `exports`. TS + some bundlers need `types` per export condition or `./package.json` export. Quick local fix: add `types` into the `.` export and include `./package.json` in exports. Example I used:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "types": "./dist/esm/index.d.ts",
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
    "default": "./dist/esm/index.js"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```

maria: Options: (1) ship the quick exports/types patch and update README to recommend `import { createClient }` (low risk); (2) longer-term: dual builds `dist/edge` (pure ESM, no node builtins) + `dist/node` and richer `exports` with `edge` and `node` conditions.

dan: CI gap — we only test Node. I can add a tiny sample-apps/edge smoke test that runs an esbuild bundle targeting webworker to catch these before publish. ci-bot suggests gating it behind `TEST_EDGE=true`.

ci-bot: Suggested pipeline step: `test:edge` runs `npm pack` and an esbuild bundle of sample-apps/edge using the packaged tarball. :white_check_mark:

shawn: I'll open the quick patch PR with the exports change + README note. I'll also start a spike for the dual-build approach (esbuild for edge, rollup for node) so we can decide publish workflow.

maria: Thanks — assign PR to me for review. Short-term patch first, dual-build spike in parallel. We'll update sample apps and docs after the PR lands. :rocket:
